servicesSub: Every visit is one dog at a time, at your place, with warm water and all the gear set up in the van.

services.title: Wash & blow-dry
services.short: A warm hydrobath, gentle shampoo and a thorough dry so the coat comes up soft and fresh.
services.long: Your dog gets a warm hydrobath with a shampoo chosen for their coat and skin, then a full blow-dry and brush so they come out soft, fluffy and smelling fresh for days. No car trip, no waiting room.

services.title: De-shed & brush-out
services.short: For spitz, huskies, collies and other double coats. Undercoat out, no knots left behind.
services.long: Double-coated breeds drop a lot of undercoat, and it ends up all over your house. A proper de-shed lifts out the loose undercoat and works through knots without shaving the coat that keeps them comfortable.

services.title: Groom & tidy
services.short: Face, feet and hygiene tidy-ups, plus full clips when they're due.
services.long: From a quick tidy of the face, feet and hygiene areas through to a full clip, Al keeps your dog looking neat between bigger grooms.

services.title: Nail trims
services.short: Calm, quick nail clips, even for dogs who usually won't allow it.
services.long: Plenty of dogs hate having their feet touched. Al takes it slowly and many owners say it's the first time their dog has stayed calm for a nail clip.

faq: Do I need to be home?
It's best if someone is home to hand your dog over and pay, but Al can work around you. Just mention it when you book.
What does the van need from me?
Nothing. The van carries its own warm water and power, so Al only needs somewhere to park near your driveway.
Can you handle anxious or reactive dogs?
Yes. Al takes time to settle each dog first, and many clients book him because their dog does better at home than in a salon.
How often should my dog be washed?
Most dogs do well every 4 to 8 weeks. Double-coated breeds benefit from a de-shed at the change of seasons.

aboutParas: Al's Dog-Wash started with a simple idea: dogs are calmer at home, so bring the wash to them.
Al works one dog at a time from a fully fitted van, with warm water, professional dryers and grooming gear on board. That means no car trips, no cages and no waiting around in a noisy salon.
He's built a loyal following across Ballarat, especially with owners of big, fluffy and nervous dogs who have struggled with groomers before.
